settings.heading: Description
settings.row_content:
A high-strength magnesium complex delivering 1,000 mg per serving across eight elemental forms of magnesium — malate among them — in a bottle of 90 capsules.

Most cheap magnesium supplements lean on a single form, usually oxide, because it is the least expensive way to put a big number on a label. A complex spreads the dose across several forms instead, which is the point of taking one at all.

Magnesium contributes to normal muscle function, normal energy-yielding metabolism, the reduction of tiredness and fatigue, normal functioning of the nervous system, normal psychological function, and the maintenance of normal bones and teeth.

settings.heading: Who It's For
settings.row_content:
For anyone whose diet is light on magnesium-rich food — leafy greens, nuts, seeds, dark chocolate, avocado — and for people who train hard and want to support normal muscle function. Many customers take theirs in the evening as part of a wind-down routine.

Follow the serving size on the label and do not exceed it. Food supplements are not a substitute for a varied and balanced diet or a healthy lifestyle. Keep out of reach of children.

Speak to your doctor before starting if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, have kidney problems, or take any medication — magnesium can interfere with the absorption of some antibiotics and bone medicines, which is usually managed by spacing the doses a few hours apart.

These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease.

settings.heading: When should I take it?
settings.row_content: With a meal, and whenever you'll remember. Most customers settle on the evening after dinner — partly habit, partly because it fits a wind-down routine.

settings.heading: Why eight forms instead of one?
settings.row_content: Magnesium is always bound to a partner compound, and that partner affects absorption and stomach comfort. Oxide is the cheapest and props up most budget labels. Spreading 1,000 mg across eight forms, malate included, means the serving doesn't rest on any single one.

settings.heading: Will it upset my stomach?
settings.row_content: Magnesium can loosen the stomach at higher doses, which is largely an oxide problem. Take it with food and a full glass of water, stick to the serving on the label, and if it doesn't agree with you, drop to a smaller serving before giving up on it.

settings.heading: Is it suitable for me?
settings.row_content: Check the label for allergens and capsule material before ordering if you're vegan or vegetarian. Speak to your doctor first if you're pregnant or breastfeeding, have kidney problems, or take medication — magnesium can interfere with some antibiotics and bone medicines, usually solved by spacing doses a few hours apart.

settings.heading: How do I store it?
settings.row_content: Somewhere cool and dry with the lid closed, out of direct sunlight and out of reach of children. No refrigeration needed.

settings.heading: Eight Forms, Not One
settings.text:
Magnesium is never sold on its own — it always arrives bound to something else, and that partner decides how well your body takes it up and how kindly your stomach receives it. Magnesium oxide is the cheapest pairing and the one most budget supplements rely on for a big label number.

This complex spreads its 1,000 mg across eight forms, including magnesium malate, so the dose does not rest on any single one. That is the whole argument for a complex over a one-ingredient tub.
